A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DetAny3D and contain complete, readable main text and supplementary Sections 6–10. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of all tables, figures, equations, and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot and in-domain detection experiments, component ablations, and appendix prompt/backbone experiments in Tables 1–5, alongside qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including all five result tables and the qualitative detection and video-generation examples.

M1.justification: The SAM/DINO architecture, 2D Aggregator, Zero-Embedding Mapping, 3D Interpreter, losses, and prompt procedures are unchanged in Sections 3 and 7.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 16-dataset DA3D coverage, held-out category and camera scenarios, and application examples. Correcting 'Omni3D++' to 'DA3D' in Section 6 is terminology cleanup, not a dataset change.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparator rows in Tables 1–2 remain identical: Cube R-CNN, OVMono3D, ImVoxelNet, SMOKE, and OV-Uni3DETR. The appendix backbone comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, AP metrics, target-aware prompting, model configurations, 80-epoch training, batch size 64, and 10% ablation subset are unchanged. Removing the generic YouTube-processing disclosure does not establish a revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Sections 4.4 and 9 retain the same component, prompt, and backbone ablations. The Sora demonstration, qualitative detection comparisons, and 3RScan annotation case study also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its experimental results.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–5 match, including Omni3D AP3D of 34.38 with ground-truth box prompts. Qualitative examples and the appendix finding of severe zero-shot degradation without intrinsic prompts are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The architecture equations, camera-ray definitions, and appendix loss formulations are unchanged. Removing an empty citation placeholder beside SILog loss in Section 7.3 does not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about promptable monocular 3D detection, zero-shot generalization, knowledge transfer, and downstream applications.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the explanations concerning 2D-prompt bottlenecks, annotation and naming mismatches, geometric knowledge transfer, and dependence on intrinsic prompts in unseen scenarios. No substantive interpretation or limitation is added or removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds a direct repository URL and replaces the abstract's project-page pointer. Sections 4.1 and 10 state that datasets retain their respective licenses; Section 10 removes the blanket CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 claim and YouTube permission/trimming details. Implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 86 referenced works and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Removing citation occurrences from the licensing paragraph does not change the cited-work set or research positioning.

P1.justification: Limited edits correct 'Omni3D++' to 'DA3D', remove an empty citation placeholder, revise resource-access wording, and shorten the licensing paragraph. Section order and the scientific narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 moves from page 6 to page 7, where Table 2 and Figure 3 are repositioned. The front-page repository line also causes text reflow. Figure content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 provides clearer repository access, consistent dataset terminology, and more coherent dataset-specific licensing guidance. These offer a limited documentation and usability gain. Removing the YouTube-processing paragraph loses some provenance detail, while the scientific methods and evidence remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish repository availability.
